facts.content: Patient presents with sudden-onset left-sided headache with visual changes, dizziness, nausea, and vomiting.
facts.source_text: CC: Sudden-onset L-sided headache with visual changes, dizziness, N/V

facts.content: The left-sided headache started this morning with approximately 4 hours duration at the time of documentation.
The headache onset was sudden.
facts.source_text: Onset: This morning; ~4 h duration; sudden

facts.content: The patient rates the headache as 6 out of 10 in severity.
The patient reports blurred vision with zigzag lines and inability to tolerate screens.
facts.source_text: Vision: Blurred with zigzag lines; cannot tolerate screens

facts.content: The patient has had two episodes of vomiting with ongoing nausea.
The patient reports dizziness that is worse with movement and prefers to keep the head still.
facts.source_text: Assoc: N/V x2; ongoing nausea; dizziness; worse with movement; prefers head still

facts.content: The patient denies limb weakness and reports walking is normal.
facts.source_text: Neuro ROS: Denies limb weakness; walking normal

facts.content: The patient took paracetamol approximately 3 hours after onset of headache with no relief.
facts.source_text: Analgesia: Paracetamol ~3 h after onset; no relief

facts.content: The patient believes pregnancy is unlikely.
The patient is concerned about having a brain tumor or stroke.
Patient has a history of kidney stones.
Patient is not taking any regular medications.
Patient reports no known drug allergies.
facts.source_text: Allergies: No known drug allergies (per pt)

facts.content: The patient's mother has migraines.
The patient's mother has hypothyroidism.
No vital signs or physical examination findings are documented.

Clinician assessment is that this first episode of acute left-sided headache with visual phenomena, nausea, vomiting, and screen intolerance without focal deficits by history is consistent with migraine.
facts.source_text: 1) Acute L-sided headache with visual phenomena, N/V, screen intolerance; first episode, no focal deficits by hx — c/w migraine

facts.content: Clinician identifies health anxiety regarding serious intracranial pathology.
facts.source_text: 2) Health anxiety re serious intracranial pathology

facts.content: Patient is advised to start ibuprofen and an over-the-counter antiemetic from the pharmacy.
Patient is advised to drink a sugary carbonated beverage such as cola.
Patient may consider using over-the-counter Migraleve if needed.
A same-day in-person review is arranged for a full neurological examination, which may be cancelled if symptoms resolve before the appointment.
facts.source_text: • Arrange same-day in-person review for full neuro exam; may cancel if symptoms resolve before appt

facts.content: Patient is instructed to contact the clinic immediately if any further problems occur before the appointment.
facts.source_text: • If any further problems before appt, contact clinic immediately
